To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have isolated two cDNAs encoding proteins which cross‐react with neurofibrillary lesions of Alzheimer disease.
two clones were isolated with anti‐NFT monoclonal antibodies and one of these encodes MAP 2 and the second encodes a protein that has not been previously described.
two cDNA clones, one encoding MAP 2 and the other encoding an unknown protein, were isolated using a monoclonal antibody to Alzheimer neurofibrilary tangles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of cDNAs encoding epitopes shared between NFT and two microtubule associated proteins.
the characterization of cDNAs encoding epitopes of SDS‐insouble neurofibrillary structures.
the isolation and characterization of cDNAs that share epitopes with Alzheimer neurofibrilary tangles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAP 2 and the 1 kb cDNAs encode two novel proteins that share epitopes with NFT.
the anti‐N FT monoclonal antibody pool is a mixture of antibodies to different proteins, including tau, which are expressed in a variety of cell lines and tissues.
these cDNAs encode epitopes shared with neurofibrillary pathology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NFT‐reactive antibodies recognize a variety of antigens in brain.
we have isolated two cDNAs encoding proteins which share epitopes with Alzheimer neurofibrillar tangles.
, in the brain, at least two different proteins, MAP 2 (80 kD) and a 40‐kD protein, share epitopes with NFT and are encoded by two distinct genes.

there are at least two proteins in the human brain that cross‐react with the antibodies that react with the NFT.
